⚑ ref AND digest ARE SEPARATE, on luthen-observability's images.json shape. A
RUNTIME cites `ref` with NO digest: containerd's CRI resolves an image by an
exact lookup on ParseDockerRef, which drops the tag from a repo:tag@digest
reference, so that form can never be a hit — measured there as a container
failing to create 48 times. The digest is the IDENTITY and lives beside the
reference, which is what a cache key wants and what a puller must not use.
⚑ THE DIGEST IS A WITNESS FROM A DIFFERENT PARTY than the builder: buildkitd
wrote it to --metadata-file as containerimage.digest. A digest computed by the
thing being attested is not an attestation.
adopted_note: ⚑ DECLARED IS NOT ADOPTED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS A FACT ABOUT THE ARTIFACTS.
This image exists and its digest is witnessed — but NOTHING IN THE TREE HAS
BEEN RENDERED IN IT. The checked-in screens were produced by the Gentoo host's
Qt and fonts. Setting adopted=true while that is so would make every recorded
action key assert a build that never happened, which is the stale-status defect
this repo exists to dissolve, arrived at from the other side.
So check_action_key reads the host as `unpinned` while adopted is false, and
names this digest as the candidate. Flip it in the SAME change that moves
render_screens into the image and re-baselines the 55 PNGs — with the
source: built on luthen 2026-09-22 by buildctl against the host buildkitd (unix:///run/buildkit/buildkitd.sock, dockerfile.v0 frontend) from oci/Containerfile; digest read from buildkitd's --metadata-file containerimage.digest
caveats: THE RECIPE IS LOOSE: apt-get resolves against a moving archive, so this digest
can be IDENTIFIED but not REBUILT. A rebuild that reuses buildkit's apt layer
yields the SAME digest, which is correct and is the point — a byte-identical
image IS the same host, and the cache is the pin doing its job. Do not add a
cache-busting build-arg; that manufactures a new host on every rebuild.
NOT PINNED AGAINST CONTAINERD's IMAGE GC. The image exports into k3s's
containerd (namespace k8s.io) and an unpinned image with no live container is
evictable — the kubelet measures imagefs usage, which a build cache inflates.
luthen measured both of its built images unpinned since first build.
⚑ AN EVICTION IS RECOVERABLE, AND THE DIGEST IS WHY. A first draft of this
file said the opposite — that a loose recipe makes eviction unrecoverable, so
the identity would survive while the ability to run the host did not. The
operator: 'eh? You have the image checksum, right?' MEASURED 2026-09-22: the
same buildctl invocation re-run under a different tag produced the SAME digest,
sha256:d1f7920a1fc02e6f…, because buildkit's cache holds the apt layer. That is
the cache being the pin, which is what it is for.
⚑ AND THE CHECKSUM'S REAL WORK IS IN THE CASE WHERE THE CACHE IS ALSO GONE. A
rebuild then resolves against a moved archive and yields a DIFFERENT digest —
which is DETECTED rather than silently accepted. A checksum does not make the
world stop moving; it converts an unrecoverable loss into a legible difference.
'I cannot get that host back' and 'I got a different host and know it' are not
the same state, and only the second one is recorded here.
THE RENDERS HAVE NOT BEEN RE-BASELINED AGAINST THIS IMAGE. The checked-in
screens were produced by the Gentoo host's Qt and fonts; this image carries
Debian trixie's. Adopting it as the render context WILL move the PNGs, the
legibility floor and the symmetry counts, and that belongs in its own commit
with the before/after measured.
